title: Mark Cuban strongly believes that manufacturing can return to the US from China
content: Mark Cuban stresses the critical need for the US to compete with China in the realms of robotics and artificial intelligence to revitalize domestic manufacturing. He believes that advancements in technology can make local production both economically feasible and sustainable. Cuban points to his venture, Cost Plus Drugs, as a prime example of how US manufacturing can lower costs.

title: Ohio couple spent $30,000 on friend's home; court revives eviction bid
content: An Ohio couple who moved into a friend's house in 2020 and spent $30,000 renovating its kitchen have lost their claim to purchase the property for $215,000. On Wednesday, an appeals court ruled that the renovations did not establish a binding purchase agreement. However, the couple may still receive compensation for the improvements, while the homeowners can pursue eviction proceedings.

title: France unrest: PM orders curfews, hints at declaring emergency; over 2,400 arrested
content: France has experienced significant unrest following protests over rising living costs and public services, resulting in violence and property damage. More than 2,400 people were arrested nationwide as rioters targeted shops, city halls, and public offices. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu instructed local authorities to consider curfews to prevent further violence while reviewing policing policies.

title: India shelves coal import plan as high global prices, weak rupee raise costs
content: India has decided not to mandate coal imports for power plants due to high international prices and a weaker rupee. Coal stockpiles have reached critically low levels at many power stations, prompting concerns about electricity shortages in the country. Policymakers are focusing on boosting domestic coal production and improving transportation to mitigate the situation.

title: US entrepreneur used AI to save time; her to-do list grew to 156 tasks
content: Morissa Schwartz's experience with her AI assistant revealed an unexpected outcome: an escalated to-do list. Instead of easing her tasks, the assistant generated more reminders and hurdles. To address this, she devised a plan to trim her task list and prioritize clear communication about challenges faced. Ultimately, Schwartz seeks to ensure her AI enhances her productivity rather than complicates it.

title: Sarah Beeny wins bid to save farmhouse on £3m estate from demolition
content: Sarah Beeny has won an eight-year planning battle to retain her Somerset farmhouse, dubbed ‘mini-Downton Abbey’. Bought for £3 million in 2018, the property was extended without planning permission. After her retrospective application was rejected in 2024 and an appeal failed in February 2025, Somerset Council approved a revised proposal allowing the farmhouse to remain.

title: Steve Ballmer gave $10mn to restore LA courts; 350 projects completed 4 years later
content: Steve Ballmer and his wife, Connie Ballmer, donated $10 million to renovate basketball courts in Los Angeles. The project successfully revamped 350 courts throughout the city, making them more accessible. The Clippers Community Courts project was completed on June 28, 2022, at the Michelle and Barack Obama Sports Center. The renovated courts have served multi-purpose functions during the Covid-19 pandemic, aiding the community.

title: Foreign traveller praises India's roads after 2,500 km journey
content: India's road network has expanded significantly, enhancing travel experiences and connectivity across various regions. A foreign visitor recently traveled over 2,500 km, showcasing the roads from Tamil Nadu to the Himalayas. Improved highways facilitate access to urban centers, pilgrimage sites, and rural areas, making journeys more exciting. Road trips allow travelers to explore lesser-known destinations that are often overlooked by traditional tourist routes.

title: 'O Captain, My Captain': Should Congress make room for Amarinder Singh again?
content: As the 2027 assembly elections approach, the Punjab Congress is strategically recalibrating its leadership. Pargat Singh steps into the role of party president, supported by Raja Warring and Charanjit Singh Channi in the campaign efforts. Meanwhile, Sachin Pilot hints at Captain Amarinder Singh's unpredictable political future amid his recent critiques of the BJP's policies on Punjab.

title: Manipur CM condemns killing of civilians, orders tighter security in vulnerable areas
content: Manipur's chief minister Y Khemchand Singh condemned the killing of three civilians by suspected militants on Monday. Protesters placed the bodies outside the chief minister's residence, prompting police to intervene. Security forces launched a combing operation to apprehend the assailants, employing sniffer dogs and helicopters for assistance. Violence also erupted a day prior in Thoubal, leaving one person dead during community clashes.

title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35M mansion faces another property review
content: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion faces fresh scrutiny as local officials continue reviewing plans for the historic lakeside estate. While the revised six-foot privacy fence received approval in September, the proposed rear landscaping remains unresolved. Neighbors have raised concerns about tree heights and potential damage to shared sewer lines. Bratenahl’s Architectural Review Board is scheduled to revisit the landscaping proposal on November 10, 2026, leaving parts of the property improvements pending.

title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf lose $3M on $23M Tiburon mansion
content: In 2006, tennis legends Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf agreed to sell their luxurious Tiburon estate for $20 million, taking a reported $3 million loss. The 3.5-acre property featured a sprawling mansion, two swimming pools, a tennis court and stunning Golden Gate Bridge views. After nearly four years on the market, the couple reduced the asking price several times. High maintenance costs and the home's dated interiors reportedly made selling difficult.

title: Watch: Calm couple, unfazed jogger defy chaos on streets of France
content: France is currently facing significant protests driven by rising living costs and deteriorating public services. While some residents appear unfazed by the chaos, many cities have witnessed violent rioting and looting. The government has implemented tighter security measures after over 2,400 individuals were arrested during recent unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has suggested localised curfews to curb further violence.

title: Odisha vs Andhra over Kotia: Naveen Patnaik turns up heat on Mohan Majhi govt

He asked whether the “Go Back Andhra” slogan was an election gimmick, as Congress and BJP leaders also weigh in.

title: India probes Pernod Ricard, Diageo over Scotch whisky imports under UK trade pact
content: Indian tax authorities are examining whether Pernod Ricard and Diageo wrongly classified bulk Scotch whisky imports for lower tariffs. The investigation follows reduced import duties under the recent India-UK trade pact that came into effect on July 15. Tax inspectors visited Pernod Ricard’s headquarters and searched Diageo’s offices regarding these classifications. Both companies claim they are cooperating fully with the authorities during the investigation.

title: Bob Barker spent nearly $1m to move 3 elephants to sanctuary in 2013
content: In a major win for animal welfare, three elderly elephants—Iringa, Toka, and Thika—have journeyed from Toronto Zoo to a sanctuary thanks to Bob Barker's generous funding of nearly $1 million. Their four-day trek concluded at the Performing Animal Welfare Society in California, where they will need time and veterinary expertise to adjust after decades of captivity. This move symbolizes hope for the future of the elephants and advocates alike.

title: Indian-origin siblings sold cookies in 2018; charity gave 100,000 books
content: Rohan and Anya Satija initiated the Let's Learn Foundation to provide books and mental health support. They began their efforts with a lemonade stand in 2018, raising awareness about educational inequalities. The foundation has since reached over 15,000 students across Texas and partnered with various organizations for resources. Their mission continues to focus on underserved communities to ensure equitable access to education.

title: Amanda Seyfried's Catskills farm is now a nonprofit animal rescue sanctuary
content: Amanda Seyfried has rejuvenated a charming 1930s farm in the Catskills, turning it into a cozy family haven and a sanctuary for rescued animals. Not only did she expand the farmhouse, but she also transformed the barn into a delightful guesthouse. As a nonprofit animal rescue, they provide a home to various animals, including horses and dogs.

title: Sold house, bought Rs 1.10 cr flat with wife; taxman rejects exemption for half amount

The replacement property was jointly registered in his and his wife's names, with the total investment of around Rs 1.10 crore. title: French unrest hits football: Marseille & Lille stores looted as clubs condemn violence

Marseille's official store on La Canebière was damaged and will remain closed for repairs, while Lille's downtown store also suffered extensive vandalism and is closed until further notice. Both clubs have condemned these acts, expressing solidarity with their employees and supporters as authorities launch cleanup operations and impose restrictions.

title: Over 50 killed as Houthis target Yemen military camp with ballistic missiles

The attack also resulted in over two dozen troops wounded, according to military officials. Following the strikes, Yemeni forces reported recapturing territory in Taiz governorate, while Houthi forces continued their offensive. In another incident, a coalition airstrike killed nine people, including children and women, in Saada.

title: Security scare at Delhi Metro: CISF jawan chases down NRI hiding ‘semi-solid substance’

The Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) noticed suspicious behavior and initiated a chase. After apprehending the individual, CISF personnel discovered a concealed suspicious substance in his undergarment. The passenger claimed to be a non-resident Indian living in Kuala Lumpur. He was subsequently handed over to the police for further investigation.

title: Asian Para Games Medal Tally: Where does India stand after a bumper 11-medal haul?

The success was rounded off with two more gold medals in athletics, placing India fourth overall in medal standings after day one.

title: Barbados-born man, 62, faces deportation after 50 years in Britain
content: Tony Hall, a 62-year-old London resident, faces deportation despite living in the UK for 50 years. His immigration issues stem from a 2001 criminal conviction for conspiracy to rob and possession of a firearm. He has lived under a deportation threat for over 14 years, reporting biweekly to the Home Office. Hall's current status leaves him at risk of homelessness as he relies on his sister for support.

title: Tiger Shroff firing case: Accused allegedly conducted reccee of his house

The accused were captured on a train trying to escape to Nepal after the attack. Local police coordinated effectively to detain the suspects at Kota railway station within a short time frame.

This meeting is suggested to take place during the upcoming APEC summit in China next month. However, Ukraine has expressed concerns about being excluded from such discussions. Ukrainian officials believe this exclusion may encourage Russian President Vladimir Putin to prolong the war.

Frustrated by rampant corruption and expensive university tuition, protesters have hurled stones and petrol bombs. In reaction, police have unleashed water cannons and tear gas to control the situation, resulting in multiple injuries on both sides. title: Asian Para Games: India win 11 medals on Day 1 as Nishad, Mona lead four-gold haul

title: ‘I am not afraid’: Sheikh Hasina vows to return to Bangladesh in December
content:
Speaking virtually at an event hosted by the Center for US-Bangladesh Relations in Washington, Hasina said it was her responsibility to return to Bangladesh.

Former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina on Monday reiterated her intention to return to Bangladesh in December, even if the Tarique Rahman-led government arrests, kills or tortures her. Speaking virtually at an event hosted by the Center for US-Bangladesh Relations in Washington, Hasina said it was her responsibility to return to Bangladesh. “I will go back to Bangladesh in December, I am not afraid. I know they can kill me, arrest me and torture me," Hasina said. “It’s my responsibility to go,” she added.
